title: Mapping from a constant coherent diagram is a limit of mapping spaces
statement: Use universes, small quasicategories, coherent functor categories, constant diagrams and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the space-valued transport and coherent mapping bifunctor $H_E:E^{\mathrm{op}}\times E\to\mathcal S$ of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], and small limits of spaces of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Let $K$ and $E$ be small quasicategories, let $F:K\to E$ be a coherent functor, and let $z\in E$. Write $\Delta_K z$ for the constant diagram. Evaluation of a coherent transformation at the vertices and simplices of $K$ induces a natural equivalence of spaces $$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(\Delta_K z,F)\simeq\lim_{k\in K}\operatorname{Map}_E(z,F(k)).$$ The right-hand diagram is $H_E(z,F(-))$, the composite of $F$ with the covariant restriction $H_E(z,-)$ of that bifunctor, whose values are naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_E(z,F(k))$. The equivalence retains all higher simplices, is natural in $z,F$, in postcomposition by functors $T:E\to E\prime$ (on the right, through the map of limits induced by the transformation $H_E(z,F(-))\to H_{E\prime}(Tz,TF(-))$ that corresponds under transport to the map of pulled-back source-fixed arrow left fibrations applying $T$ to arrows), and in restriction along functors $K\prime\to K$. Empty $K$ is allowed; its right side is the terminal space. No limits in $E$ are assumed.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.13(3), 3.2.3(4) and Example 3.2.4(3): general coherent mapping-space calculation underlying the relative-limit clause; statement extracted by the agent. General reference wanted: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, sections 5.1.2-5.1.3.

proof.text: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ containing the small quasicategories $K,E$, and form the space category in a containing universe. Let $H_E$ be the coherent mapping bifunctor of the transport classification and put $H=H_E(z,F(-)):K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$; this is exactly the diagram $F_{z,F}$ of the constant-source section comparison, a coherent space-valued diagram and not a diagram of component sets. The constant-source section comparison, applied with $J=K$, $p=F$, $x=z$, gives an equivalence $a:M\simeq N$, where $M=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(\Delta_Kz,F)$ and $N=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(\Delta_K*,H)$, through the section space $\Gamma_K(q_{z,F})$. It identifies an entire coherent transformation with its family of arrows $z\to F(k)$ and all their higher compatibilities. The size hypotheses hold because $K,E$ are $\mathcal U$-small, so $E$ is $\mathcal U\prime$-small with $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces; the comparison also supplies a small Kan model for $M$.

source.place: Agent application of the existing constant-source comparison; Subsection 7.4.1, especially the section/transformation comparison of Proposition 7.4.1.14.

proof.text: By the small-limit assertion choose a limiting cone $\lambda:\Delta_KL\to H$ in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. The mapping-space cone criterion applied in this space category, with testing object $*$, says that $b:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(*,L)\to N$, $u\mapsto\lambda\circ\Delta_Ku$, is an equivalence. Here we use the cone criterion itself, rather than the representable limit formula with its right-hand limit. Apply the first equivalence of the point-cocone criterion with its indexing simplicial set equal to $\Delta^0$ and $Y=L$. Since $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,L)=L$, it gives the natural point-evaluation equivalence $e:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(*,L)\simeq L$. Consequently $c=b\circ e^{-1}:L\simeq N$ is an equivalence. Only a limit in spaces has been chosen, never a limit in $E$.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.1.1 and the paragraph following it; small limits of spaces. Example 4.6.7.7 (06QR) for point evaluation.

proof.text: Take $c^{-1}a:M\simeq L$. To identify this equivalence, first compose $c$ with evaluation at any vertex or simplex of $K$. Its value on a point $\ell$ of $L$ is the corresponding component of $\lambda(\ell)$, by the formula $b(u)=\lambda\circ\Delta_Ku$ and the point-evaluation description of $e$. This is an equality of coherent families, since $\lambda$ is a transformation on the whole indexing simplicial set. The comparison $a$ has exactly the same evaluation description for a transformation in $M$. Thus the inverse $c^{-1}$ sends that family to its point of the limit, proving that the displayed equivalence is the evaluation-induced comparison claimed in the statement. The cone criterion and the constant-source comparison are equivalences of spaces, so this argument retains every parameter simplex.

source.place: Agent identification of the comparison obtained from Proposition 7.4.1.1 with evaluation; no extra comparison lemma is asserted.

proof.text: Naturality in $z,F$ and restriction $v:K\prime\to K$ holds for $a$ by the constant-source comparison. For the postcomposition clause let $T:E\to E\prime$ and $H\prime=H_{E\prime}(Tz,TF(-))$. Applying $T$ to arrows gives a map over $K$ of the pulled-back source-fixed arrow fibrations, $A_{z,F}\to A_{Tz,TF}$, $(k,h)\mapsto(k,Th)$: $Th$ is an arrow from $Tz$ to $TF(k)$, and this commutes with all simplicial operators. By the transport mapping-space equivalence for these representatives, this vertex of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(A_{z,F},A_{Tz,TF})$ is a transformation $\tau_T:H\to H\prime$, the one named in the statement, and by compatibility with composition, composition with $\tau_T$ on $N$ corresponds to postcomposition $s\mapsto Ts$ on section spaces $\Gamma_K(q_{z,F})\to\Gamma_K(q_{Tz,TF})$. On the other side an $n$-simplex of $M$ is $\sigma:K\times\Delta^{n+1}\to E$, and its section is $h=\sigma\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times\rho_n)$; since $T(\sigma\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times\rho_n))=(T\sigma)\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times\rho_n)$, the first comparison commutes strictly with $T$, which is the functor-naturality of the pinch comparison applied to $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E\prime)$. Hence $a$ commutes with postcomposition by $T$ on every simplex.

source.place: Agent naturality calculation using the explicit pinch/arrow formulas and transport of the source-fixed arrow fibration; Subsection 7.4.1.

proof.text: Now compare $c$ with $c\prime:L\prime\simeq N\prime$, built in step 2 from a limiting cone $\lambda\prime:\Delta_KL\prime\to H\prime$. The cone $\tau_T\circ\lambda$ with apex $L$ corresponds, by the cone mapping-space criterion for $\lambda\prime$ with testing object $L$, to a map $\phi:L\to L\prime$, unique up to a contractible choice, with $\lambda\prime\circ\Delta_K\phi\simeq\tau_T\circ\lambda$ as whole coherent cones; this is the induced map of limits. By the formula $b(u)=\lambda\circ\Delta_Ku$ of step 2 and the point evaluations, composition with $\tau_T$ on $N$ sends $c(\ell)=\lambda(\ell)$ to $\tau_T\lambda(\ell)\simeq\lambda\prime(\phi(\ell))=c\prime(\phi(\ell))$, on every parameter simplex. Restriction along $v$ is treated in the same way, with the restricted cone $\lambda v$ and the limiting cone of the restricted diagram. Therefore $c^{-1}a$ has all the claimed naturalities. Restriction is the usual map from a limit to the limit of the restricted diagram; it need not be an equivalence.

source.place: Agent: universal property of the limiting cone of step 2 applied to the transformed cone; Proposition 7.4.1.1.

proof.text: If $K=\varnothing$, its functor category has exactly one simplex in each degree, so $M$ is a point. The small-limit assertion and the cone criterion give the terminal space for the empty limit, and all constructions above give its unique comparison. For $K=\Delta^0$ the comparison is the identity of the usual mapping space. For $K=\Delta^1$ it encodes an arrow $z\to F(0)$ together with its coherent image in $F(1)$, with no unjustified product over vertices. If a Hom value is empty, there is no coherent point family; both sides can be empty and none of the cited assertions required nonempty mapping spaces. If $E$ is empty there is no object $z$, so the statement has no such instance.
